newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises petrol prices 10 pct, diesel 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises petrol prices 10 pct, diesel 9 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday raised petrol and diesel prices for the second time in as many weeks after the lev fell sharply against the dollar.
"Petrol prices will rise by an average of 9-10 percent and diesel fuel prices by 8.7 percent, effective from Friday," a government statement said.
Petrol prices will rise to 141-186 levs per litre from 129-170 levs while diesel fuel price will rise to 112 levs from 103 levs.
The government usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
The lev was trading at 355 to the dollar on Thursday from 270 on November 14 when petrol prices were increased by an average 18 percent and diesel by 14 percent.

The government decided to keep unchanged the prices of central heating and low-grade coal during winter months after thousands of Bulgarians gave up central heating at their homes due to unaffordably high prices.
In January, when the lev traded at around 70 per dollar, average petrol prices were 27.25 levs per litre and diesel was 19.50 levs per litre.
Cumulative consumer price inflation for the first 10 months of 1996 was 195 percent, official statistics showed.
Bulgaria imports more than 80 percent of raw materials for its energy sector and pays for the supplies after it exchanges levs for dollars.
The prices of electricity, coal and heating include value added tax of 22 percent.
